t: Read in the name of your Lord Who created,
created man from a clinging clot.
Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous,
taught man what he did not know[1].
when he deems himself to be self-sufficient.
Indeed, to your Lord is the return.
Have you seen the one who prevents[1]
What if this [slave] is rightly guided,
How about the one who denies and turns away[1]?
Does he not know that Allah sees all?
No indeed; if he does not desist, We will surely drag him by the forelock[1]
So let him call his associates;
We will call the wardens of Hellfire[1].
No indeed; do not obey him, but prostrate and draw near [to Allah].
f: [1] These five verses (1-5) are the first ever verses revealed of the Qur’an. The Prophet (ﷺ) was retreating at a cave in the outskirts of Makkah when the angel Gabriel appeared before him, and ordered him to read. Since the Prophet (ﷺ) was unlettered, he would respond, “I cannot read.” Gabriel would then squeeze him tightly and order him again to read. Ultimately, Gabriel said to him: “Read in the name of your Lord …”.
[1] i.e., Abu Jahl was a pagan leader of the Makkah who was an arch-enemy of Islam.
[1] Abu Jahl abused the Prophet (ﷺ) when he prayed in the Holy Mosque.
[1] From what the Prophet (ﷺ) has brought and does he not fear Allah?
[1] It alludes to the frontal lobe of the brain, where reasoning is processed.
[1] i.e., the coarse, rigorous, and harsh angels assigned for the Hellfire.
